Sam (support): FYI customer is hitting intermittent 502/504s on /v1/embeddings with very large batches. First reports ~09:11 UTC. Trace snippets below, sending customer repro steps.
Priya (eng-sre): On it — any request ids or sample payloads?
Sam (support): Sample req ids: r-175A-0x9, r-175B-0x2f. Customer says they sent ~1200 vectors in one POST.
Sam (support): Logs pasted: ```[edge] 2025-05-14T09:11:02Z req=r-175A upstream_error=upstream reset before headers code=RST_STREAM```
Carlos (obs): Dashboards show a sharp conn_pool_exhaustion spike on midproxy between 09:10-09:12 UTC. CPU on midproxy pods jumped to 95%. Auth cache miss rate also doubled in same window. Link: https://obs.example/graphs/edge-burst (internal)
Luca (eng-runtime): That pattern smells like long-lived streams + high concurrency from one tenant. Are they chunking the body or sending one huge content-length?
Sam (support): Customer repro curl (they provided): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input": ["<vector>" x1200]}'``` They said single POST, not chunked.
Priya (eng-sre): Envoy logs show repeated `HTTP/2 stream concurrency limit reached` followed by `upstream connection closed` and then 502 at edge. Also saw `pool overflow` from our midproxy. Recent infra change?
InfraBot: Deploybot: canary rollout of ingress-keepalive-tuning v2 completed 2025-05-13T22:03:10Z by @deploybot
Luca (eng-runtime): We rolled keepalive max idle streams lower in that deploy to avoid stale fds. That reduces headroom for many concurrent h2 streams — explains pool exhaustion when a single tenant opens 1200 concurrent streams.
Priya (eng-sre): Confirmed correlation: the keepalive tuning decreased `max_concurrent_streams` fallback behavior. When large single requests arrive without chunking, midproxy holds many streams which bloat connection tables and cause upstream resets.
Sam (support): Customer impact: majority of their calls get 502 or 504 within first 30s of burst, then occasional success as a few tokens get through. They're asking for immediate mitigation.
Luca (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigations: 1) Ask customer to reduce batch size (<=100) or enable chunked uploads. 2) Roll back keepalive param in ingress to previous value (quick revert). 3) Add server-side guardrail to reject >256 items with 413 + helpful error while we patch.
Priya (eng-sre): I'll prepare a revert PR to revert `ingress-keepalive-tuning` and schedule a canary to validate within 15m.
Carlos (obs): I'll pin dashboard alert thresholds and create a filter to surface tenant r-175A/r-175B. Also capturing full trace: trace=trace-1753334444-abcd for deeper analysis.
Sam (support): I pushed workaround to customer: reduce batch to 100 and retry with exponential backoff. They can also use our batch-split helper in SDK (temp flag). Customer acknowledged, but needs SLA fix.
Luca (eng-runtime): Longer term: enforce batch size at API gateway, add backpressure responses (429/Retry-After) for too many concurrent streams, and add server-side chunking recommendation in docs. I'll open an RFC after we triage.
Priya (eng-sre): Revert PR opened: #5234. Rolling canary now. Will monitor conn_pool and RST rates.
InfraBot: CI: revert PR #5234 passed CI and is deploying to canary cluster.
Carlos (obs): Canary shows connection errors dropped to baseline and CPU normalized after revert at 09:28 UTC. Midproxy pool usage returned to normal.
Sam (support): Customer confirmed lower error rate after following workaround; they'll resume production tomorrow once we finalize fix.
Priya (eng-sre): Action items: 1) Revert keepalive tweak (done). 2) Add server reject for oversized embed batches (Luca). 3) Doc update & SDK guardrail (Luca). 4) Support follow-up with ACME (Sam).
Luca (eng-runtime): I'll own RFC and the server-side guardrail. ETA EOW.
Sam (support): Thanks all. Closing triage for now — reopening if we see new bursts from other tenants. :thumbsup:
